coverageNote: Fresh source-only audit. Enumerated `/home/rob/Projects/WeJammin/.memory/wiki/specs/ideation/24-trust-safety-disputes/` from disk: 54 Markdown files across the domain unit (3 files, including 24.09) and eight sub-domains — 24.01 (7), 24.02 (8), 24.03 (8), 24.04 (6), 24.05 (6), 24.06 (5), 24.07 (5), and 24.08 (6). All 54 files were read from the ideation tree; no prior 24 audit report was used. A relative-link resolver checked 551 Markdown links and found 1 absent target. Pending-marker review followed linked questions and source-domain contracts before recording findings: correctly owned questions and explicit downstream deferrals are not reported as gaps.

scoring.naRationale: This is an ideation-layer audit rather than an IA implementation spec. Feature enumeration is authored in the domain tree, not as per-unit IA-shard feature lists. User-flow detail is assessed where a unit writes a concrete state/flow contract; it is N/A for aggregate units that only establish taxonomy or cross-cut relationships. The remaining dimensions were assessed for access, data ownership, cross-unit contracts, failure modes, depth, and implementation determinacy.

findings.claim: The appeals flow requires an appellant to submit ‘any new evidence’ and a reviewer to use it, while the domain-wide Case Evidence Locker forbids every party write path and defines the messaging thread as the only sanctioned post-hoc context channel. No contract defines what an appeal’s new evidence is, where it is stored, whether it is immutable and party-visible, or how it stays distinct from contemporaneous evidence.
findings.evidence: 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.02-appeals-internal-complaints.md:54 says the subject files an appeal ‘with a reason and any new evidence’; :56 says the reviewer examines the original 24.09 bundle ‘plus new evidence’; :70 requires new evidence for a repeated appeal. CONTRADICTED BY 24.09-case-evidence-locker.md:36-40 (‘None has write access’ and ‘There is no upload evidence affordance anywhere’), :180 D-02 (‘No party may write to a bundle’), and :159 DT-04, which redirects post-hoc context only to the captured messaging thread. The appeal file has no decision or open question owning an appeal-supplement object or reconciling it to the bundle.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must choose between rejecting new evidence despite the appeal flow, appending party material to an immutable bundle, or creating an unmentioned supplemental evidence store with its own chain of custody, access, retention, and appeal-repeat semantics.
findings.failureScenario: A suspended musician obtains a new, exculpatory document after the original decision. One build refuses it because 24.09 permits no upload; another appends it to the case bundle, defeating the contemporaneous-evidence guarantee; a third stores it in an unaudited attachment table. The three outcomes change both due process and what evidence a later reviewer can trust.

findings.claim: The CSAM path is required to have break-glass-only access and never disclose its basis to the subject, but it also writes a legal hold onto the shared 24.09 evidence bundle. The shared locker grants a suspended party read access to their own open case and says all adjudication children consume the same bundle. No exception or redacted-view contract reconciles those access rules for the generic suspension review.
findings.evidence: 24.08-illegal-content-legal-process/24.08.01-csam-detection-preservation-reporting.md:21 and :70 require no user visibility and only a generic suspension-review path; :121 says preservation is a hold on the 24.09 bundle. trust-safety-disputes-cx.md:20 makes 24.09 the one bundle for all adjudication children, while :325 says break-glass is the sole CSAM access and :371-379 require a generic appeal that never exposes the underlying CSAM case. CONTRADICTED BY 24.09-case-evidence-locker.md:31-34 (each persona reads its own case bundle), :103 (both parties and the adjudicator open the same PII-scoped bundle), and :115 (read access to a party’s own open case persists while suspended). No source names a sanitized appeal bundle, an access-denied exception, or a permissible evidence projection.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementation must invent whether a falsely actioned subject receives the CSAM-held bundle, a redacted derivative, or no evidence view at all. Each option changes prohibited-content exposure, the secrecy of detection, and the meaningfulness of the promised suspension review.
findings.failureScenario: A perceptual-hash false positive triggers a generic suspension. If the normal 24.09 rule applies, the subject or ordinary appeal reviewer can access CSAM-linked evidence, violating break-glass isolation and non-disclosure. If it does not apply, the appeal has no stated evidence view and becomes indistinguishable from an unsupported assertion.

findings.claim: The Block/Mute cross-cut says propagation must be correct at every call site, but leaves a block arriving after a ticket sale, gear purchase, or booking as an explicitly unresolved choice between voiding, refunding, or mediated completion. The issue has no linked open question, owner, or target despite deciding both safety behavior and payment/fulfilment outcomes.
findings.evidence: 24.06-personal-safety-threat-response/24.06-personal-safety-threat-response-cx.md:65-69 requires a single restriction fact to propagate across domains and calls propagation failure dangerous; :74-76 then states ‘an existing obligation (an amp already bought, a ticket already sold) when a block lands mid-transaction. Void, refund, or complete through an intermediary? Unresolved’. 24.06-personal-safety-threat-response-index.md:61-67 contains only Q-01 (locatability), Q-02 (emergency services), and Q-03 (meeting duty of care); none owns this transaction state. A fresh source-wide search found no source defining the stated void/refund/intermediary choice.
findings.forcedInvention: Every transaction surface must choose whether the safety restriction cancels a paid obligation, creates a refund, exposes parties through completion, or requires a third party. Those rules cannot be safely inferred from a generic block operation.
findings.failureScenario: A buyer is restricted by a seller after paying for a gear listing that requires local collection. One build forces an in-person handoff despite the restriction; another refunds and strands the seller with a sold item; another creates an intermediary flow without authority or compensation rules. The user’s safety expectation and the money outcome differ materially.

findings.claim: The entity-appeal edge case links to a nonexistent Domain 01 directory, breaking the contract that determines who may appeal a sanction on behalf of an organisation.
findings.evidence: Fresh link resolution found 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.02-appeals-internal-complaints.md:69 targets `../../01-identity-profiles/`, which is absent. The current source directory is `../../01-identity-profiles-organizations/`. The broken link sits in the rule that says an entity appeal requires an appeal-capable mandate and that co-owner filings merge into one case.
findings.failureScenario: A downstream author following the entity-appeal rule cannot reach the mandate source and may invent a separate appeal-authority model or skip the co-owner conflict constraint entirely.

findings.claim: Several current edge-case rows retain unqualified `[PENDING]` or completed-stage pending markers after their questions were either resolved or re-owned elsewhere. The marker format no longer distinguishes live work from stale prose, so it weakens the domain’s otherwise careful traceability.
findings.evidence: 24.04.03-buyer-seller-protection-programs.md:57 says a producer’s unpaid-delivery case is pending ‘see Q-02’, but the same file’s Q-02 at :112 is resolved to Payments/Escrow. 24.07.03-deceased-incapacitated-succession.md:58 leaves the deceased-producer/unreleased-stems case pending, while Q-03 at :111 resolves it through 07.03.03’s role-derived vault access. 24.05.04-pre-release-leak-detection-response.md:61 leaves label-staff leakage pending although Q-03 at :126 owns it at `/create-prd`; 24.06.01-harassment-stalking-doxxing.md:58 retains a completed-step marker even though 18.04.02 and the show-production CX already route dietary-data lawful basis and retention to `/create-prd-security`. These are representative examples from the fresh marker review, not new product questions.
findings.failureScenario: A later pass reopens a settled payment or succession rule, while a genuinely live issue is mistaken for resolved because both appear as bare pending rows. The result is duplicated design work and inconsistent downstream contract references.
